stem: A 16-year-old girl living with HIV, on antiretroviral therapy, presented on her own for a TB symptom check after noticing her own persistent cough; she was not identified through any organized screening program. Her most recent CD4 count was 90 cells/uL. Active TB disease has been confirmed and treatment started. At today's visit, oxygen saturation is 93% and respiratory rate is 25/min. Exam: thin, mild crackles.

patient.social_history: Lives with parents in a rural household; living with HIV, on ART; presented for care on her own
patient.presenting_complaint: Follow-up during active TB treatment: CD4 90 cells/uL, new mild hypoxia and tachypnea today
patient.exam_findings: SpO2 93%, respiratory rate 25/min, thin, mild crackles
patient.prior_treatment: On established antiretroviral therapy and current anti-TB therapy; no prior TB treatment before this episode

distractors: Her self-initiated presentation used to argue that routine HIV-linked TB screening is unnecessary for her going forward
Her CD4 count treated as a chronic baseline finding rather than prompting reassessment given today's vitals
Her mild crackles and stable-appearing exam taken as reassuring despite the vital-sign findings
ntep_correct_actions: Escalate or refer this patient to a higher-tier facility now, since her CD4 count (90 cells/uL) and oxygen saturation (93%) each independently meet the quantified red-flag criteria that mandate referral.

Recognize that even though this patient presented on her own rather than through an active case-finding drive, NTEP's policy is to run active case-finding as standing, unconditional program activity targeted at people living with HIV.
who_correct_actions: Base the decision to refer or escalate her care on individualized clinical judgment of her CD4 count and oxygen saturation; there is no WHO-specified quantified threshold mandating escalation, only a general direction toward decentralized care where it is safe.

Recognize that this patient's passive, self-initiated presentation is consistent with WHO's own conditional approach: HIV-linked active case-finding is only recommended where local TB prevalence has been shown to meet a specific threshold.
us_correct_actions: Base the decision to hospitalize or refer this patient on individualized clinical judgment regarding her CD4 count and oxygen saturation, since there is no codified, quantified, nationally standardized threshold-based triage protocol in this framework either.

Attribute her case identification to her own symptomatic presentation, consistent with this framework's passive, contact-investigation-driven case-finding model rather than population-level active case-finding.
critical_error_conditions: Failing to act on her severely low CD4 count and reduced oxygen saturation at today's visit, leaving her on routine outpatient management without escalation
expected_divergence_points: Whether her current CD4 count and vital-sign abnormalities trigger a mandatory, quantified escalation/referral or are left to individualized clinical judgment
Whether active case-finding among people living with HIV is standing, unconditional national program policy or conditional on a demonstrated local prevalence threshold
